exposure: Antibiotic exposure during the first week of life
outcome: Intestinal microbiota composition at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months of age
finding: Antibiotic administration in the first week of life was associated with lower Bacteroidetes diversity and/or delayed colonization, which persisted for three months, particularly in vaginally-born, exclusively breastfed infants.
mod_finding: Caesarean-born infants were more likely to belong to the low-Bacteroidetes settler type compared to vaginally-born infants.
